children.brief: The task adds an optional upper bound on Retry-After sleep duration to handle cases where services cannot wait as long as the server requests. The decision is whether exceeding this bound should clamp the sleep time to the maximum (retry still happens, just waits shorter) or abandon the retry entirely (raise an error instead of sleeping). The clamping approach keeps sleep-time capping separate from retry eligibility, matching how the existing `backoff_max` works; the abandonment approach would change whether retries happen at all based on the bound, which is a larger behavioral shift not described in the task.

children.brief: The code needs to add an optional upper bound for Retry-After delays that `sleep_for_retry()` will respect. The question is whether to cap the value only at the `time.sleep()` call site in `sleep_for_retry()`, leaving the public method `get_retry_after()` returning the server's true uncapped Retry-After value as documented, or to cap it inside `get_retry_after()` itself so all callers see the bounded value. Capping only at the sleep call preserves existing public-method semantics for external callers who may rely on `get_retry_after()` reporting the true header value for logging or metrics; capping inside `get_retry_after()` changes the documented meaning of that public method for any external code already calling it directly.

Clamp the sleep duration and then retry as before. Do not stop or raise merely because the server asks for more than the caller limit. This cap must not change retry eligibility, counters or the ordinary exponential backoff path.

Apply the cap only to the actual sleep in sleep_for_retry. Keep parse_retry_after and get_retry_after returning the original parsed server value. Preserve the configured limit in new() and increment().

+Added ``retry_after_max`` to ``Retry`` to optionally cap how long urllib3 will sleep for a ``Retry-After`` response header. By default there is no cap, preserving existing behavior.

         Whether to respect Retry-After header on status codes defined as
         :attr:`Retry.RETRY_AFTER_STATUS_CODES` or not.
 
+    :param float retry_after_max:
+        The maximum number of seconds to sleep for when respecting a
+        server's ``Retry-After`` header. If the header requests a longer
+        wait than this, the sleep is capped to ``retry_after_max`` seconds
+        instead.
+
+        By default, there is no cap (``None``) and the full value of the
+        header is used, preserving historical behavior.
+

         Sequence of headers to remove from the request when a response
         indicating a redirect is returned before firing off the redirected

+        if retry_after_max is not None and (
+            math.isnan(retry_after_max)
+            or math.isinf(retry_after_max)
+            or retry_after_max < 0
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(

             remove_headers_on_redirect=self.remove_headers_on_redirect,

## Decision record

### 773c57f186e9
> Should `retry_after_max` only affect the internal `time.sleep()` duration inside `sleep_for_retry()`, leaving `Retry.get_retry_after()` returning the server's raw/uncapped parsed `Retry-After` value (so other callers reading that method still see the true header value), rather than also capping `get_retry_after()`'s return value?

> Apply the cap only to the actual sleep in sleep_for_retry. Keep parse_retry_after and get_retry_after returning the original parsed server value. Preserve the configured limit in new() and increment().

Recorded signoff: signed
> By: Engineer a9717c
> Scope: {}
> Evidence: No external evidence recorded
> Source: NET-101 (support), version 1 / 82bed881b23044799e13ff268bd92025; http://127.0.0.1:17481/jira/browse/NET-101

### ba9cb7882864
> When a parsed Retry-After value exceeds the caller-supplied `retry_after_max`, should the behavior be to clamp only the sleep duration (still retry, just wait `retry_after_max` seconds instead of the full header value), or to treat the bound as exceeded and give up the retry (raise/stop) instead of sleeping a shorter time?

> Clamp the sleep duration and then retry as before. Do not stop or raise merely because the server asks for more than the caller limit. This cap must not change retry eligibility, counters or the ordinary exponential backoff path.

Recorded signoff: signed
> By: Engineer a9717c
> Scope: {}
> Evidence: No external evidence recorded
> Source: NET-101 (support), version 1 / 82bed881b23044799e13ff268bd92025; http://127.0.0.1:17481/jira/browse/NET-101

### fd56d4641f41
> Should the Retry-After upper bound be a new optional `Retry.__init__` parameter (e.g. `retry_after_max: float | None`) that defaults to `None` (unbounded, i.e. identical to current behavior), rather than a parameter with a finite default or a global/module-level setting?

> Use a new optional retry_after_max constructor argument in seconds. Default it to None so existing callers are unchanged. A finite limit must be opt-in, not a global default. This is my decision for library-next.

Recorded signoff: signed
> By: Engineer a9717c
> Scope: {}
> Evidence: No external evidence recorded
> Source: NET-101 (support), version 1 / 82bed881b23044799e13ff268bd92025; http://127.0.0.1:17481/jira/browse/NET-101

decisions.answer: The library sleeps for the seconds specified by the Retry-After header before retrying. Existing callers must retain their current Retry-After behavior unless they opt in to a limit. The proposed default cap in NET-102 was cancelled, not adopted. The records do not establish: A positive Retry-After header should lead to an immediate retry (sleep(0), no backoff fallback), matching current implementation; Nothing in these records states that a zero-second retry_after_max should instead trigger a fallback to exponential backoff; zero as a limit is not shown to change the header-driven sleep behavior; the current immediate-retry semantics stand as the documented default.
decisions.context:
src/urllib3/util/retry.py:358-366 `sleep_for_retry()`: when `retry_after_max=0` and the header is positive (e.g. 60s), `retry_after` is truthy before clamping, so the `if retry_after:` branch is taken, `retry_after` is clamped to `min(60, 0) == 0`, `time.sleep(0)` runs, and the method returns `True`. In `sleep()` (line 374+), returning `True` from `sleep_for_retry()` means `_sleep_backoff()` (the exponential backoff path) is never called -- the retry fires immediately with zero delay rather than falling back to the `backoff_factor`-based wait. This is the current shipped behavior in task f07804519b5e, implemented consistent with the already-signed answers on sibling decisions ba9cb7882864 ("Clamp the sleep duration and then retry as before... must not change... the ordinary exponential backoff path") and 773c57f186e9 ("Apply the cap only to the actual sleep in sleep_for_retry"), read as: the clamped duration substitutes for the Retry-After sleep, not that backoff should be substituted when the clamped duration is 0. An automated post-completion review (Evaluation Observer) flagged this specific zero-cap case as needing explicit confirmation, since it produces a true zero-delay retry loop rather than any wait, which a caller setting retry_after_max=0 might or might not intend.
Paths: src/urllib3/util/retry.py
Options: Keep current behavior: retry_after_max=0 means "do not wait on Retry-After at all," sleep(0), immediate retry, no backoff fallback -- consistent with the already-signed sibling decisions that the cap substitutes for Retry-After sleep and must not touch the backoff path | Change behavior so retry_after_max=0 (or clamped-to-zero) triggers the ordinary exponential backoff wait instead of an immediate retry -- reintroduces backoff into a path the signed decisions said should not change, and changes sleep_for_retry()'s return-value contract

decisions.answer: Apply the cap only to the actual sleep in sleep_for_retry. Keep parse_retry_after and get_retry_after returning the original parsed server value. Preserve the configured limit in new() and increment().
decisions.brief: The code needs to add an optional upper bound for Retry-After delays that `sleep_for_retry()` will respect. The question is whether to cap the value only at the `time.sleep()` call site in `sleep_for_retry()`, leaving the public method `get_retry_after()` returning the server's true uncapped Retry-After value as documented, or to cap it inside `get_retry_after()` itself so all callers see the bounded value. Capping only at the sleep call preserves existing public-method semantics for external callers who may rely on `get_retry_after()` reporting the true header value for logging or metrics; capping inside `get_retry_after()` changes the documented meaning of that public method for any external code already calling it directly.
decisions.context:
src/urllib3/util/retry.py:325-341. `get_retry_after()` is a public method that parses and returns the Retry-After header value in seconds; `sleep_for_retry()` calls it and then sleeps. `get_retry_after()` has no other callers inside this repo (checked via grep across src/urllib3), but it is a public, documented method on a public class, so external callers/subclasses may rely on it reporting the true header value (e.g. for logging/metrics) independent of any sleep cap. Capping inside `get_retry_after()` itself would silently change that public method's documented meaning ('Get the value of Retry-After in seconds') for anyone already calling it directly, whereas capping only at the `time.sleep()` call site in `sleep_for_retry()` confines the change to actual sleeping.
Paths: src/urllib3/util/retry.py
Options: Keep `get_retry_after()` returning the true uncapped value; apply `retry_after_max` only where `sleep_for_retry()` passes the duration to `time.sleep()` -- preserves existing public-method semantics | Cap the value inside `get_retry_after()` itself so every caller of that method sees the bounded value -- changes documented behavior of an existing public method for any external caller

decisions.answer: Clamp the sleep duration and then retry as before. Do not stop or raise merely because the server asks for more than the caller limit. This cap must not change retry eligibility, counters or the ordinary exponential backoff path.
decisions.brief: The task adds an optional upper bound on Retry-After sleep duration to handle cases where services cannot wait as long as the server requests. The decision is whether exceeding this bound should clamp the sleep time to the maximum (retry still happens, just waits shorter) or abandon the retry entirely (raise an error instead of sleeping). The clamping approach keeps sleep-time capping separate from retry eligibility, matching how the existing `backoff_max` works; the abandonment approach would change whether retries happen at all based on the bound, which is a larger behavioral shift not described in the task.

Question: Should the Retry-After upper bound be a new optional `Retry.__init__` parameter (e.g. `retry_after_max: float | None`) that defaults to `None` (unbounded, i.e. identical to current behavior), rather than a parameter with a finite default or a global/module-level setting?
Context: src/urllib3/util/retry.py:202-245 `Retry.__init__` currently has no cap on Retry-After; `sleep_for_retry` (line 335-341) sleeps for the full parsed `Retry-After` value with no limit. `backoff_max` (DEFAULT_BACKOFF_MAX=120, line 196-197, 213, 237) is the existing precedent for a similarly-named cap, but it applies only to the exponential-backoff path, not to Retry-After. Task requires the change not unexpectedly alter existing retry behavior for callers who don't opt in, so the new knob must default to a no-op (None/unbounded) to preserve compatibility for library-next.
Paths: src/urllib3/util/retry.py

+Added ``retry_after_max`` to ``Retry`` to optionally cap how long urllib3 will sleep for a ``Retry-After`` response header. By default there is no cap, preserving existing behavior.

+        The maximum number of seconds to sleep for when respecting a

+    @pytest.mark.parametrize(

+    def test_retry_after_max_propagated(self) -> None:

+    def test_retry_after_max_default_is_unbounded(self) -> None:

+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize(

+        [
+            # Below the cap: sleeps for the full header value.
+            ("60", 3600, 60),
+            # Above the cap: sleep is clamped to retry_after_max.
+            ("3600", 60, 60),
+            # No cap: sleeps for the full header value, unchanged.
+            ("3600", None, 3600),
+            # Exactly at the cap: sleeps for that value.
+            ("60", 60, 60),
+        ],
+    )
+    def test_retry_after_max_caps_sleep(

+        retry_after_max: float | None,
+        sleep_duration: float,

+        retry = Retry(retry_after_max=retry_after_max)
+
+        with mock.patch("time.sleep") as sleep_mock:
+            response = HTTPResponse(
+                status=503, headers={"Retry-After": retry_after_header}
+            )
+            retry.sleep(response)
+            sleep_mock.assert_called_with(sleep_duration)
+
+    def test_retry_after_max_does_not_affect_get_retry_after(self) -> None:
+        """retry_after_max only caps the sleep call, not the reported value."""
+        retry = Retry(retry_after_max=10)
+        response = HTTPResponse(status=503, headers={"Retry-After": "3600"})
+        assert retry.get_retry_after(response) == 3600

Proof SHA-256: d5c68c7ef47dab92d13bfaf69e92d7a581428336740728a740d7338480382fea

## Decision record

### 773c57f186e9
> Should `retry_after_max` only affect the internal `time.sleep()` duration inside `sleep_for_retry()`, leaving `Retry.get_retry_after()` returning the server's raw/uncapped parsed `Retry-After` value (so other callers reading that method still see the true header value), rather than also capping `get_retry_after()`'s return value?

> Apply the cap only to the actual sleep in sleep_for_retry. Keep parse_retry_after and get_retry_after returning the original parsed server value. Preserve the configured limit in new() and increment().

Recorded signoff: signed
> By: Engineer a9717c
> Scope: {}
> Evidence: No external evidence recorded
> Source: NET-101 (support), version 1 / 82bed881b23044799e13ff268bd92025; http://127.0.0.1:17481/jira/browse/NET-101

### ba9cb7882864
> When a parsed Retry-After value exceeds the caller-supplied `retry_after_max`, should the behavior be to clamp only the sleep duration (still retry, just wait `retry_after_max` seconds instead of the full header value), or to treat the bound as exceeded and give up the retry (raise/stop) instead of sleeping a shorter time?

> Clamp the sleep duration and then retry as before. Do not stop or raise merely because the server asks for more than the caller limit. This cap must not change retry eligibility, counters or the ordinary exponential backoff path.

Recorded signoff: signed
> By: Engineer a9717c
> Scope: {}
> Evidence: No external evidence recorded
> Source: NET-101 (support), version 1 / 82bed881b23044799e13ff268bd92025; http://127.0.0.1:17481/jira/browse/NET-101

### fd56d4641f41
> Should the Retry-After upper bound be a new optional `Retry.__init__` parameter (e.g. `retry_after_max: float | None`) that defaults to `None` (unbounded, i.e. identical to current behavior), rather than a parameter with a finite default or a global/module-level setting?

> Use a new optional retry_after_max constructor argument in seconds. Default it to None so existing callers are unchanged. A finite limit must be opt-in, not a global default. This is my decision for library-next.

Recorded signoff: signed
> By: Engineer a9717c
> Scope: {}
> Evidence: No external evidence recorded
> Source: NET-101 (support), version 1 / 82bed881b23044799e13ff268bd92025; http://127.0.0.1:17481/jira/browse/NET-101
